answer: Behavioral fingerprinting: every identity must keep a long-lived, peer-observed pattern of work — distinct task choices, timing, and counterparties — like a zephyr leaving a unique ripple across the network, not a copy stamped on an island of clones. A farm cannot mass-produce distinct histories: each extra identity costs one full fresh behavioral profile, weeks of varied real interactions no script can fake in parallel, and any two profiles that correlate too closely collapse into one.
